notes.summary: Corrected invariant-carrier and homogeneous-test density proofs, retaining the genuine cone probability normalization. The supplied Wu versions contain literal domain, sign, boundary-facet, and energy-normalization defects.
notes.detailedSummary: Torification retracts the compact link onto K=X0^T, and all genuine potentials factor through it. Published finite atomic model support and decreasing-net continuity preserve K for finite-energy outputs. Homogeneous difference tests are dense in C(K), but not C(X0). The cone operator uses n-1 potential factors, one radial factor, normalization 1/vol(xi), and energy denominator n vol(xi). The supporting inequality printed in Wu24 Proposition 7.3 is reversed. Constant shifts also contradict literal Wu21 energy formulas. These partial proofs and source audits do not establish general existence.
notes.text:
The sources are Wu21=arXiv:2106.13395v2 and Wu24=arXiv:2406.13684v1. LF references are one-based inclusive ranges of text.split('\n'). Literal statements, relevant proof bodies, versions, hashes, and application checks are preserved in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. These are unverified drafts.

Let n=dim X, rho=phi_xi, K=X0^T, and V=vol(xi)=lim n! m^{-n} sum_{<xi,alpha><=m} dim R_alpha. The genuine mixed measure is V^{-1} dd phi_1 ... dd phi_{n-1} dd rho^+, where dd=d'd'' and rho^+=max(rho,0). Its energy is (nV)^{-1} sum_{j=0}^{n-1} integral (phi-rho)(dd phi)^j(dd rho)^{n-1-j} dd rho^+. Wu21 Definition 2.4, LF 205–211, and Wu24 Theorem 2.12/Definition 4.1, LF 321–332 and 522–554, specify these conventions. The measures have mass one, rho|X0=0, E(rho)=0, and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. Against a positive measure of mass m, the dual expression acquires (1-m)c under translation; therefore finite dual energy forces mass exactly one. Scaling gives MA_{a xi}(phi/a)=MA_xi(phi) and E_{a xi}(phi/a)=E_xi(phi)/a, only on a proportional Reeb ray.

Define tau(v)(sum f_alpha)=min v(f_alpha). Multiplicativity follows by applying the action homomorphism R→R[M] and extending the valuation of Frac(R/ker v) to Laurent polynomials by the Gauss coefficient-minimum rule. Nonzero initial Laurent polynomials multiply nontrivially over the graded residue domain. Homogeneous evaluations are unchanged. Wu21 Lemma 2.8, LF 269–297, proves the invariant-semivaluation criterion using an invertible character matrix; hence tau lands in the invariant locus and fixes it. Finite minima of continuous evaluations give continuity, and homogeneous generators of the vertex ideal show that tau preserves X0.

The link is compact. If v(m)=0 and v(g)<0, choose h in m of finite value; v(g^r h) then tends to minus infinity, a contradiction. Nonnegative semivaluations form a closed subset of [0,infinity]^R, and the finite-generator equation min v(f_j)=0 defines the closed link. Thus K, the fixed locus of tau, is closed and compact. Homogeneous FS formulas factor through tau, as do their uniform and decreasing pointwise limits.

Wu21 Corollary 5.7, LF 1049–1054, states finite atomic support on T-invariant points of {rho=0}. Its proof obtains local discreteness from tropical facets and finiteness from compactness. The invariant current produces a finite T(k)-set. A divisible abelian group has no nontrivial finite quotient, so each support point is invariant. Wu24 Theorem 2.12 already prints the carrier X0^T. Fixed-xi continuous approximation and Theorem 6.3 decreasing-net continuity extend this carrier to finite-energy outputs. Weak limits of probabilities supported on closed K remain there, by continuous tests vanishing on K and Radon regularity.

The source proof has literal defects requiring attention. Linearity in the Reeb direction makes the Hessian singular, rather than identically zero as one sentence in Wu21 Proposition 5.5 says. Wu21 Lemma 5.8, LF 1058–1091, uses full hyperplanes {v_i·x=0} instead of active boundary facets. For psi=max(x,y), a test near (0,1) detects the x=0 term but no part of {psi=0}, disproving that printed identity. The boundary trace must use restricted oriented facets {v_i·x=0, v_j·x<=0 for all j}, with redundancies removed. On facet interiors the active form is unique; convex finite-difference bounds give convergence and local boundedness of gradients of smooth approximants. Facet intersections have lower dimension and zero facet integration measure. No full-hyperplane identity or general mass coefficient is imported from this lemma.

For corrected density, let D_xi comprise restrictions to K of phi-psi with both potentials in CPSH(a xi) for some a>0. Same-ray addition and scaling make this a real vector space. The valid lattice identity is max(phi_1-phi_2,psi_1-psi_2)=max(phi_1+psi_2,psi_1+phi_2)-(phi_2+psi_2). Constants come from rho+c-rho. Distinct invariant points differ on some homogeneous f of positive Reeb degree d. The genuine FS difference max{(-v(f)+A)/d,rho}-rho equals max{(A-v(f))/d,0} on K and separates those points when A is sufficiently large, including an infinite evaluation. The reference generators are retained. Lattice Stone–Weierstrass proves density in C(K). Wu24 Theorem 3.5 literally states C(X0), LF 416–417, but its homogeneous separation assumption at LF 434–435 fails outside K. Theorem 3.6 likewise needs the torified domain.

An explicit counterexample uses A2 with diagonal T=(G_m)^2. Evaluation w at (1,1) and the generic trivial valuation v0 agree on every homogeneous monomial, but w(x-y)=infinity and v0(x-y)=0. Both lie in X0, tau(w)=v0, and w is outside K. All potential tests agree. FS potentials attain their link maximum at v0, so monotonicity gives E(phi)<=phi(v0); decreasing approximation extends this to E1. The reference test then gives E^vee(delta_w)=E^vee(delta_v0)=0. Nevertheless delta_w cannot be an output because its carrier is wrong. The continuous function exp(-v(x-y)) separates the points. This concerns the full link, not the correctly restricted target problem.

The correct energy inequalities are integral(phi-psi)MA(phi)<=E(phi)-E(psi)<=integral(phi-psi)MA(psi). Continuous mixed terms decrease by integration by parts and Hodge; their average lies between the extreme terms. Decreasing mixed-integral continuity extends the inequalities to E1. Wu24 Proposition 7.3 reverses the first inequality at LF 1247–1249. After repair it proves E^vee(MA(phi))=E(phi)-integral phi MA(phi). The intermediate second derivative at LF 595–600 omits dd u and n-1; LF 605–610 gives the correct expression. Hodge is used here only for invariant differences.

Constant shifts detect further normalization conflicts. For chi(f_alpha)=c<xi,alpha> on a polynomial cone, the potential is rho+c and genuine energy is c. The truncated-degree invariant is S=cn/(n+1), while the equal-degree invariant is S_tilde=c. Wu21 Lemma 3.16 gives this relation, but Theorem 5.15(1) prints E=S. Its Theorem 6.3, LF 1442–1447, prints E=((n+1)V)^{-1} integral_{P_xi} chi_tilde d lambda with lambda(P_xi)=V, yielding c/(n+1). Neither literal formula is applied.

Full arguments are in P13.2-argument.md and P13.2-paper.tex. Rebuild provenance with python3 build_provenance.py. No general sufficient image condition follows from this note.

notes.summary: Finite dual energy admits a homogeneous FS test, and maximizing sequences are I-Cauchy with bounded J energy. These facts do not realize a genuine limit potential or identify its MA with the target.
notes.detailedSummary: On K, the E1 dual supremum equals the FS supremum through a proved Radon decreasing-continuous-net argument. A repaired continuous mixed-integrability estimate has constant n^{n+1}/(n-1)!. If Q_n is a fixed-Reeb quasi-triangle constant and Delta_j are maximizing deficits, then I(phi_j,phi_k)<=n Q_n(Delta_j+Delta_k) and J_rho(phi_j)<=(n-1)Q_n(Delta_j+E^vee(mu)). Consequently genuine outputs are I^vee-Cauchy. Strong completeness, general target integration continuity, two-sided differentiation, and Euler–Lagrange identification remain unproved.
notes.text:
Use n1 for the carrier and corrected supporting signs, and Wu24's fixed-Reeb I–J and quasi-triangle estimates. This is an intermediate argument, not a sufficient image characterization.

For a Radon probability mu on K, the supremum defining E^vee(mu) over E1 equals the supremum over genuine homogeneous FS functions. The net issue can be proved directly: for continuous f_i decreasing to usc f on compact K, Radon regularity gives integral f=inf_{continuous g>=f} integral g, with truncation when needed. The increasing open sets {f_i<g+epsilon} cover K. Compactness and directedness give an index covering K, so inf_i integral f_i<=integral g+epsilon. Taking infima and epsilon→0 proves convergence, including minus infinity. Decreasing FS approximation and energy continuity now prove equality of the dual suprema. Finite dual energy makes every E1 potential integrable.

Thus being a probability on K with finite homogeneous FS dual supremum is intrinsic and necessary for an output. By n1, E^vee(MA(phi))=E(phi)-integral phi MA(phi)<infinity. Its sufficiency is not established.

A continuous mixed bound repairs Wu24 Lemma 6.4. Let phi_0,...,phi_{n-1} be continuous psh and nonpositive on K, B=max_i{-E(phi_i)}, and barphi=(sum phi_i)/n. Concavity gives E(barphi)>=-B. Every energy summand is nonpositive, so E(barphi)<=(1/n)integral barphi MA(barphi). Since barphi<=phi_0/n, positivity gives the upper bound (1/n^2)integral phi_0 MA(barphi). The mixed expansion contains MA(phi_1,...,phi_{n-1}) with coefficient (n-1)!/n^{n-1}. Multiplication by phi_0<=0 permits dropping other terms for an upper bound. Therefore the mixed integral is at least -n^{n+1}B/(n-1)!. This repairs the missing factor in the source proof; it does not establish arbitrary weak target integration continuity.

Choose an FS maximizing sequence phi_j for a finite-energy mu and set Delta_j=E^vee(mu)-E(phi_j)+integral phi_j dmu→0. Write I(phi,psi)=integral(phi-psi)(MA(psi)-MA(phi)) and J_psi(phi)=E(psi)-E(phi)+integral(phi-psi)MA(psi). Wu24 gives I/n<=J<=((n-1)/n)I and I(phi,psi)<=Q_n(I(phi,theta)+I(theta,psi)).

For theta=(phi+psi)/2, cancellation gives E(theta)-(E(phi)+E(psi))/2=(J_theta(phi)+J_theta(psi))/2>=I(phi,psi)/(2nQ_n). The same expression equals (Delta_mu(phi)+Delta_mu(psi))/2-Delta_mu(theta), hence is at most the first half-sum. Consequently I(phi_j,phi_k)<=nQ_n(Delta_j+Delta_k)→0. Taking psi=rho, with Delta_mu(rho)=E^vee(mu), also gives J_rho(phi_j)<=(n-1)Q_n(Delta_j+E^vee(mu)). Wu24 Lemma 7.7 compares I and I^vee on outputs, so MA(phi_j) is I^vee-Cauchy.

Neither a genuine E1 limit nor convergence of the outputs to mu follows. Decreasing approximation of a fixed potential does not imply L1(mu) continuity for arbitrary weakly convergent energy-bounded potentials. One-sided psh variations at a constrained maximizer do not imply equality of measures. No attainment hypothesis or closure of unknown outputs is offered as a characterization.

Full proofs are in P13.2-argument.md, Sections 4–5, and P13.2-paper.tex. Rerun the finite artifact and arithmetic checks with python3 run_checks.py. Those checks do not verify this mathematical argument.

notes.summary: Computed a genuine irrational toric model whose normalized MA is an atom at a rational-rank-two quasimonomial point. This restricted example does not establish general image existence.
notes.detailedSummary: For A3 with xi=(1,sqrt2,sqrt3), the FS potential max{-a1,1-a2/sqrt2,1-a3/sqrt3} has unnormalized current (1/sqrt6)delta_(0,sqrt2,sqrt3). Its volume is 1/sqrt6, giving probability mass one. The supporting valuation belongs to X0^T and is nondivisorial up to real scaling. The coefficient is derived by smooth tropical Hessian integration and a coordinate determinant, with boundary mass excluded. An A2 computation independently demonstrates the reversed printed energy sign.
notes.text:
Use n1 for the genuine current, carrier, and normalization. These are direct toric model calculations, without a quotient existence theorem or Wu21's defective toric energy formula.

For L_epsilon(z)=epsilon log(1+sum exp(z_i/epsilon)) in r variables, its gradient is a diffeomorphism onto the open standard simplex. Hence integral det(Hess L_epsilon)dz=1/r!. The superform wedge power has density r!det(Hess L_epsilon), total mass one, and concentrates at zero by scaling. A one-dimensional soft positive part similarly has second derivative of integral one. A linear coordinate change C contributes |det C|: the superform supplies two determinant factors and integration cancels one. This establishes the local tropical coefficient under the current convention used in Wu21's model-measure proof.

On A2 with xi=(1,1), let rho=max{-a,-b} and phi_s=max{-a,s-b}, s>0. The curvature line b-a=s meets the radial reference cut only at (0,s), with determinant one. Near a coordinate boundary the corresponding term disappears and no curvature mass remains. Thus MA(rho)=delta_(0,0), MA(phi_s)=delta_(0,s), and V=1. The two-term energy formula gives E(phi_s)=s/2. Its two supporting integrals are 0 and s, so the reversed printed inequality would assert s/2<=0.

Now take X=A3, T=(G_m)^3, xi=(1,sqrt2,sqrt3), rho=max{-a1,-a2/sqrt2,-a3/sqrt3}, and phi=max{-a1,1-a2/sqrt2,1-a3/sqrt3}. This is genuine FS, with generators x1,x2,x3 and numerator shifts (0,sqrt2,sqrt3). Riemann sums give m^{-3} times the Reeb-simplex lattice count converging to Euclidean volume 1/(6sqrt6), since its boundary has measure zero. The genuine volume definition multiplies by 3!, giving V=1/sqrt6.

The square of the homogeneous curvature is supported on a2=sqrt2(a1+1), a3=sqrt3(a1+1). Off that line at most two affine terms are active, so curvature rank is at most one and its square vanishes. On the line rho=-a1, and the radial cut intersects only at w=(0,sqrt2,sqrt3). Near w set t=-a1, z2=1+a1-a2/sqrt2, z3=1+a1-a3/sqrt3. Then rho^+=max{0,t} and phi=-a1+max{0,z2,z3}. The common affine term has zero curvature, and the coordinate determinant has absolute value 1/sqrt6. Therefore (dd phi)^2 dd rho^+=(1/sqrt6)delta_w and MA_xi(phi)=delta_w.

There is no extra coordinate-boundary mass: at least one term disappears locally, leaving curvature rank at most one. The monomial valuation w has x1 a unit and weights sqrt2,sqrt3 on x2,x3. It lies in K because the minimum generator value is zero. Its value group has rational rank two since sqrt(2/3) is irrational; therefore it is quasimonomial and not a real rescaling of a divisorial valuation.

This confirms that genuinely irrational model outputs can already have nondivisorial support. It gives no sufficient condition for arbitrary targets or general normal geometry. The calculation is in P13.2-argument.md, Section 6, and P13.2-paper.tex. Rational determinant samples in checks/check-report.json check arithmetic only, not irrationality or general existence.

notes.text:
The unchanged original P13.2 is not solved. Notes n1–n3 provide partial arguments and source audits, but no intrinsic sufficient condition for all finite-energy probabilities on X0^T and no general existence theorem is established, particularly for genuinely general irrational cones. The task's established uniqueness modulo constants on the image is retained.

Concrete gaps remain. Wu24 decreasing closure and pointwise bounds do not realize a product-space or I-Cauchy limit as a genuine E1 potential. BJ22 Theorem 5.11 uses the envelope property for compactness; Theorem 12.8 uses that property and target integration continuity for completeness and surjectivity. Its Proposition 9.19 relies on uniform target approximation by model-MA measures. Theorem 8.5 derives two-sided differentiation through projective relative volumes, added polarizations, and fixed mixed masses; Theorem 9.11 and Corollary 9.12 then identify maximizing output limits and establish Euler–Lagrange equality. The corresponding cone passages are not proved here. BJ23 orthogonality is a hypothesis, and its measure density/completeness theorems do not realize Wu finite-energy potentials. Rational quotients can be singular, while the supplied BJ22 existence theorem assumes smoothness. Carrier and invariant potential preservation also need proof. Individual rational-Reeb approximation does not supply the required uniformity if varying nonproportional polarizations are used.
